messages:
maya: noticing a p99 and p95 latency bump starting ~02:10 UTC on the h100 pool after the driver bump this morning. left a profiler dump in /tmp/trace-1799.tar.gz :thinking:

tom: saw that — quick glance shows kernel_choice switched for a lot of short sequences (<=64) from vectorized-attn -> fallback-slowpath. KV cache hit rate seems stable but per-token CPU spikes. attaching a flamegraph link: https://internal/redwood/fg/1799

leo: can we confirm whether autotuner table changed, or if the driver changed kernel perf numbers causing misrank? i ran the autotune dry-run on one host and it returned a different score matrix for small-seq kernels.

maya: paste from profiler: ```
hot_kernel: attn_vec_v2 (latency=0.42ms, score=0.68)
fallback: attn_block (latency=1.1ms, score=0.92)
post-driver: observed attn_vec_v2 latency change -> 0.78ms on same hardware
```

tom: that matches — driver scheduling seems to have increased context-switch or kernel-launch latency, harming short-kernel throughput. autotuner picks are now favoring attn_block due to higher variance in the vec path's tail latency.

ops_sre: infra-bot flagged increased 99th on the pool and opened INC-1198. We currently have canary traffic split 5% -> 100% on new driver. Reverting to previous driver is possible but requires node rotation; ETA ~45m for staged rollback.

jess: what's the rollback risk? will the autotuner then flip back and forth? worried about oscillation if we just revert driver without pinning kernel picks.

leo: good point — short-term rollback will restore prior latency but autotuner may re-evaluate and pick vec path again once metrics normalize, which is fine. bigger concern is config churn: we should pin a conservative kernel preference in the serving runtime until we ship an autotuner fix. propose env: REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF_SHORT_SEQ=attn_block to force stable behavior.

maya: agree. immediate plan: 1) ops to start staged driver rollback on 2 nodes as canary, 2) eng-runtime to set REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF_SHORT_SEQ=attn_block for the affected pool, 3) collect autotune logs and instrument per-kernel latency histograms, 4) open a follow-up to fix scoring (maybe use median+tail weighting).

tom: I can push the kernel-pref flag now (hot) to canary pool, will post command. ```/bin/redwoodctl set-pool-config h100-pool --env REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF_SHORT_SEQ=attn_block```

ops_sre: starting rollback on h100-canary-3 -> h100-canary-4. will stream logs here. expected 45m to 1h to see cluster-wide impact.

infra-bot: INC-1198 created by ops_sre; participants: maya, tom, leo, jess, ops_sre. Severity: S2.

jess: once rollback is confirmed, do we want a temporary autotuner safeguard? like require +2% improvement for vec path to be promoted for seq<=64 for next 24h.

leo: yes — add a hysteresis: require sustained improvement over a sliding 30m window and penalize high tail variance. I'll draft a PR for autotuner heuristics and push tests.

maya: thanks. action owners: ops_sre = rollback, tom = kernel-pref rollout, leo = autotuner PR, jess = risk signoff. update thread when canary shows effect. :thumbsup:

ops_sre: rollback started (job id roll-1799). streaming: "replacing driver -> nodes drained -> driver 535 restored". watching metrics.

maya: initial numbers look promising — p95/p99 trending down on canary. leave the kernel-pref on for now until autotuner PR lands.

tom: pushed kernel-pref to canary and half of staging. command output: OK (applied to 6 hosts).

leo: opened PR #4723 with tests + new scoring that adds tail-variance term; requesting review from jess and maya.

jess: reviewing now. if green, we should roll to staging and hold for 24h before prod rollout.

maya: excellent. will keep this thread updated. we should also add a short runbook entry for "kernel misrank after driver bump" in eng-runtime playbook.

ops_sre: rollback completed on canary; metrics improved. propagating to remaining nodes in controlled batches. expected full completion in ~2h.
